data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes when it is a rule-target blocker whose necessity was established by a planted failure that the author then treated as proof of the test's independence. The 3-of-26 result is the number of mutations that fall outside the rule-target route authorized by the acceptance record \u2014 mutations that no guard catches because no rule was ever written to target them, and the shown-to-fail-first installation only amplifies this by making the test's authority derive from the planted failure rather than from the code.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3 surviving mutations are shown to be within the rule-target route and still survive, the route-based explanation fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py's lost mutation is in a module with no rule-target route, the loss is a routing gap not an installation artifact.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If an ordinarily-guarded module catches a mutation outside its rule-target route, the route does not determine the result.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shown-to-fail ritual is applied to mutations chosen without reading the acceptance record, the manufactured-failure confound is removed and the ratio should change.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The acceptance record authorizes a rule-target route where guards are installed against specific mutations. When a mutation is planted and the test shown failing, the test's authority is established by that failure. But the failure was manufactured: the mutation was chosen by a model that had read the acceptance record, so the test was never independent of the rule-target structure. The 3 surviving mutations are those outside the rule-target route \u2014 they were never the subject of a rule, so no test was ever shown failing for them, so no test constrains them. The 1-of-9 compile.py loss is a mutation that would require a rule-target route but was never assigned one under the shown-to-fail-first installation. The 4/4 to 6/7 spread reflects how many rule-targets were authored per module, not the quality of the guards.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
